title: Serverless with Cloudflare Workers
text: These questions check that you understand how a Worker handles requests, can use D1 and Wrangler, and can protect a public API.

tasks.text: What does a Worker's fetch function return?
Which D1 call returns one row, or null if there is none?
What does npx wrangler d1 execute garden-signups --local --file=./seed.sql do?
choices: Loads the seed data into the real, online database
Loads the seed data into a local copy of the database, used by wrangler dev

tasks.text: Why was DELETE /signups/:id safe enough on your own computer but not on Workers, and how does a cancel code fix it?
tasks.answer: Locally only you could reach it; online anyone can, and sequential ids are easy to guess, so anyone could cancel everyone's sign-ups. A cancel code is a long random token (crypto.randomUUID) given only to the person who signed up, required to cancel, so it can't be guessed.

tasks.text: An assistant moving your API to Workers dropped a rule and renamed a field. Why did that happen, and what should you do when moving code to a new platform?
tasks.answer: In a new chat it didn't know the original rules or field names ("the same as before" means nothing to it), so it made assumptions. Give it the old code or a complete list of rules and names, and test the new version against the original design.

tasks.text: A Worker routes by splitting the path. Write a function route(method, pathname) that returns "list" for GET /shifts, "one" for GET /shifts/:id, "signup" for POST /shifts/:id/signups, "cancel" for DELETE /signups/:id, and "none" otherwise. Then write testRoute, which logs route("GET", "/shifts"), route("POST", "/shifts/6/signups"), route("DELETE", "/signups/13") and route("GET", "/members").

Set up the lesson's Worker locally with wrangler dev. In a new chat with your updated learner profile, paste the Worker code and ask for a new route, GET /shifts/:id/spots, returning { spotsLeft }. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did the assistant follow your new rule, or did you give it the code first? (3) Add the route, test it with a script for shift 6 and an unknown shift, and paste the output. (4) If you have a Cloudflare account, deploy it and test the public address too.
tasks.answer: Full credit: rule compliance noted; route tested locally with correct results (e.g. 3 spots left for shift 6 before sign-ups; 404 unknown); deployment reported if attempted. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
